newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai 97 C/A deficit seen easing to 7.5 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Thai 97 C/A deficit seen easing to 7.5 pct of GDP.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Wednesday he expected the current account deficit to narrow to at least 7.5 percent of gross domestic product in 1997 from 8.0 percent in 1996.
Amnuay said weak exports broke an earlier seven-month downtrend. He also said inflation, which was 5.8 percent in 1996, eased in recent months.
"I believe the current account deficit could be brought down at least 0.50 percentage point this year (from the 1996 level of 8.0 percent)," he said.

The minister said he expected his conservative fiscal and monetary policies to gradually produce positive results that would hopefully convince Moody's Investors Service not to downgrade the country's long-term sovereign debts.
Moody's said in mid-February it was reviewing Thailand's A2 foreign currency sovereign ceilings for bonds and bank deposits for possible downgrade.
Moody's is sending two representatives to Bangkok early next month.
Amnuay said Thailand could not afford to be complacent and would continue adopting measures to revive its ailing property sector as well as strengthen its financial institutions.
